name: Flint
title: Investor Renovation Contractor in Flint, MI | Genstone
metaDescription: Flint renovation contractor for investors: Civic Park, Mott Park and Woodcroft homes repiped, rewired and scoped against thin comps before you commit capital.
intro: Flint is a market where the purchase price is rarely the hard part. Houses are inexpensive, and the Genesee County Land Bank and tax-foreclosure auctions keep a steady supply moving. The hard part is making the rehab budget fit a finished value that may be modest, while dealing with houses that have often been vacant, stripped of copper or damaged by fire and weather. A rehab that would be a sensible upgrade in Grand Blanc can sink a deal inside the city limits. Genstone Construction starts with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review that prices the work on the specific house and tests it against what the finished property is likely to appraise or rent for. If the numbers hold, the project runs from an itemized scope and draw schedule under one field manager, with licensed local trades handling the work and the city permits. Nothing is due upfront, and money is released only for finished stages.
housingStock:
Flint’s houses were built for the people who built cars. As General Motors and its suppliers expanded in the 1910s and 1920s, the city added tens of thousands of homes in a short span, and much of that stock still stands. The most famous example is Civic Park on the northwest side, a planned neighborhood developed around 1919 by a GM-affiliated housing company, with curving streets and rows of modest frame colonials, bungalows and gambrel-roof houses built from a small set of plans.

Closer to downtown, Carriage Town preserves Flint’s oldest residential fabric, with Italianate and Queen Anne houses from the carriage-making era of the late nineteenth century. The Grand Traverse District and Central Park hold early twentieth-century foursquares and Victorians, many of them divided into apartments over time. Woodcroft Estates, on the south side, was built for executives and managers in the 1920s and 1930s and has large brick Tudors and colonials on wooded lots. Mott Park, near Kettering University, and the College Cultural area near the UM-Flint and Mott Community College campuses offer 1920s through 1950s brick and frame homes that remain popular with owner-occupants.

On the east and north sides, much of the housing is small frame worker homes from the 1920s through the 1940s, with block or poured basements, original wood windows and many layers of paint. Common issues across the city include knob-and-tube circuits, corroded galvanized water lines, cast-iron stacks, root-filled clay laterals, asbestos on old heating pipes and lead paint. Long vacancy has added a second layer: missing plumbing and furnaces, fire damage and roof failures that let water into the structure for years. On many east side blocks, the house next door is gone, which leaves side walls, chimneys and foundations exposed to weather they were never meant to face.

commonIssues.title: Interior plumbing after the water crisis
commonIssues.body: After the 2014 switch to Flint River water, corrosive water released lead from service lines and plumbing. The city has since replaced lead and galvanized service lines across most of Flint, but the pipes inside a house are the owner’s concern. Galvanized interior piping that sat downstream of a lead line can hold lead-bearing scale. For both tenants and buyers, a full repipe in PEX or copper with new fixtures is often the single most persuasive item in a Flint rehab.

commonIssues.title: Stripped and scrapped houses
commonIssues.body: Many vacant Flint homes have been entered and stripped of copper pipe, furnaces, water heaters, wiring and aluminum. A house that looks intact from the street may have no working systems at all. Budget for a complete mechanical package when the basement shows cut pipes or empty mounting brackets. Securing the property quickly after purchase matters too, because a house under renovation with new copper and equipment is an attractive target until it is occupied.

commonIssues.title: Fire and smoke damage
commonIssues.body: Vacant structures in Flint have a long history of fires, and houses next to burned properties sometimes carry smoke, heat or water damage from firefighting. Charred framing, melted wiring and smoke odor in plaster can be hidden behind paint and paneling. When a property has any sign of past fire, we inspect the attic and wall cavities closely and price structural repair, odor sealing and full rewiring where needed rather than spot patches.

commonIssues.title: Foundations in older worker housing
commonIssues.body: Many of the 1920s houses in Civic Park and on the east side were built quickly and economically. Block and poured basements may show cracking, bowing and seepage, while porches and rear additions sometimes sit on shallow piers that have heaved with frost. Sill plates can rot where the soil is high against siding. Checking the basement walls and the joints between the main house and its additions is one of the first steps in our Flint pre-offer reviews.

commonIssues.title: Thin comps and appraisal limits
commonIssues.body: In large parts of Flint, there are few recent arm’s-length sales of renovated homes, and many transactions are cash sales of distressed property. That makes it hard for an appraiser to support a high after-repair value, even for excellent work. Before scoping a deep renovation, we look at the sales an appraiser would likely use. In many neighborhoods, the smart rehab is durable and complete rather than upscale, and the return comes from rent rather than resale.

investorMarket:
Flint rewards investors who know the city block by block. The neighborhoods with steady owner-occupant demand, including Woodcroft Estates, Mott Park, College Cultural, Glendale Hills and parts of Carriage Town, support resale strategies because buyers there use mortgages and comparable sales exist. Those areas suit careful flips and FHA 203(k) sales to first-time buyers, provided the finish level matches what nearby homes have sold for.

Across much of the north and east sides, resale values are low enough that most investors choose to hold. Rental demand is real, drawing on workers at the hospitals, the GM truck plant, local government and the colleges, and on households that cannot buy. Rents can be strong relative to purchase price, but repair costs do not shrink to match house prices, so the rehab must be efficient and durable.

The Genesee County Land Bank has long been a major source of inventory and is widely regarded as a pioneer of the land bank model. Its sales often carry rehab requirements and occupancy deadlines. Inner-ring suburbs such as Burton, Flint Township and Grand Blanc offer post-war housing and more consistent comps, and many Flint-area investors balance a portfolio between the city and those communities, using the city for cash flow and the suburbs for steadier values.
permits:
In the City of Flint, building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are issued through the city’s Building and Safety Inspections Division. Almost any rehab beyond paint and flooring needs at least one trade permit, and a scrapped house typically needs all of them, along with coordination with Consumers Energy to restore gas and electric service and with the city’s water department to restore water. Each permit has rough and final inspections, and finals should be closed before the house is sold or leased.

Before you lease a renovated house, confirm with the city what registration or inspection currently applies to rental property, and keep records of your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, handrails, egress and heating. Federal lead disclosure rules apply to virtually every Flint rental and sale because of the age of the housing, and lead-safe work practices are required when painted surfaces are disturbed.

The suburbs have their own building departments. Burton, Grand Blanc, Flint Township and other communities each issue their own permits. Because a Flint mailing address can sit in a township, our field manager checks which office has authority over the parcel before pricing permits, then keeps each inspection sign-off with your project records.
climate: Flint has a classic mid-Michigan climate: cold, cloudy winters with regular snowfall, many freeze-thaw cycles and summer heat with humidity and thunderstorms. For renovations, winter is the season of frozen pipes. A vacant house with the gas off can lose its plumbing in a single cold weekend, and many Flint purchases happen with utilities disconnected. Restoring heat or winterizing should happen immediately after closing. Freeze-thaw cycles crack concrete steps, porches and driveways and loosen mortar in chimneys. Spring brings snowmelt and heavy rain that test basements, gutters and grading, and low areas near the Flint River and its tributaries can see standing water. Exterior painting, roofing, masonry and concrete are best scheduled from late spring to early fall, while interior work can continue year-round once the house is heated.

faqs.q: Is it worth renovating houses inside Flint city limits?
faqs.a: It can be, when the purchase price, rehab budget and rent or resale value line up. Flint houses are inexpensive, but rehab costs do not drop to match. Neighborhoods like Woodcroft Estates, Mott Park and College Cultural have stronger owner-occupant demand, while other areas work better as rentals. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the specific house and compares it with realistic values, so you can decide with numbers rather than hope.

faqs.q: Should I replace the interior plumbing in a Flint rental?
faqs.a: In most older Flint houses, yes. The city has replaced service lines across much of the city, but interior galvanized pipes and older fixtures remain the owner’s responsibility. Replacing them with PEX or copper, new valves and new faucets removes a concern tenants and buyers raise often. It also solves low water pressure and leaks common in century-old galvanized lines. We document the repipe so you can show it to future tenants and buyers.

faqs.q: Do you work on Genesee County Land Bank houses?
faqs.a: Yes. Land Bank properties range from houses that need modest updates to shells that need everything. Sales often include rehab requirements and timelines. We scope the work against those conditions so the money you spend counts toward the commitments in your purchase agreement. Because many Land Bank homes have been vacant for a long time, we focus first on roofs, plumbing, heating and electrical, which usually drive the budget.

faqs.q: How do you protect a Flint renovation from theft?
faqs.a: Securing the house is part of the plan from the first day. That can mean replacing doors and locks, boarding or securing basement windows, avoiding leaving new equipment exposed before it is installed and scheduling deliveries close to installation. Genstone Field Services can also provide periodic property checks. Once the furnace, water heater and copper are installed, getting the house occupied quickly is one of the best protections.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Flint, MI | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Flint fix and flip contractor: Woodcroft, Mott Park and College Cultural homes rehabbed to match real comps, with documented repipes buyers want to see.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Flint
fix-flip.intro: Flipping in Flint is a narrow game, and it is played on a handful of streets. The houses that resell to owner-occupants with mortgages are concentrated in neighborhoods such as Woodcroft Estates, Mott Park, College Cultural and Glendale Hills, plus pockets of Carriage Town. Outside those areas, a beautiful renovation can still appraise below its cost. Genstone Construction helps you decide whether a flip makes sense before you buy. The free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the work and compares it with the sales an appraiser would actually use. When a deal makes sense, we write a scope that spends on what Flint buyers check first, such as new interior plumbing, safe wiring and a dry basement, and we run the job with one field manager, licensed local trades and draws tied to finished work.

sections.h2: Picking a Flint house that can resell
sections.body:
The first decision in a Flint flip is the street, not the kitchen. In Woodcroft Estates, the brick Tudors and colonials sit on wooded lots and attract buyers who would otherwise look in Grand Blanc. Mott Park, near Kettering University and the golf course, has well-kept 1930s and 1940s homes that appeal to faculty, hospital staff and young families. College Cultural, near the UM-Flint and Mott Community College campuses, has a mix of styles and an established owner base. Glendale Hills and the better blocks of Carriage Town also see renovated homes sell.

Even within those neighborhoods, condition and recent sales vary widely. A house that backs onto vacant lots or sits next to a boarded property can appraise noticeably lower than a similar house two blocks away. Before we write a scope, we look at the specific sales an appraiser would likely choose and match the finish to them. If the closest renovated sales are modest, the plan should be too.

sections.h2: What a Flint buyer’s inspector looks for
sections.body:
Many Flint buyers have lived through the water crisis or know people who did, and their first questions are about the pipes. Showing that the service line has been replaced and that the interior plumbing is new PEX or copper, with new fixtures and a new water heater, addresses that concern directly. We keep the documentation, including photos of the repipe and any records of the service line replacement, so your listing agent can share them.

Beyond plumbing, inspectors focus on the electrical panel and wiring, the furnace, the roof and the basement. Older Flint homes often have mixed wiring, with knob-and-tube or cloth-insulated circuits connected to newer panels. Basements may show cracks or water staining, especially in homes with high grading or failing gutters. Correcting those items before listing prevents long inspection reports, renegotiations and canceled contracts. In Flint, where buyer pools can be small, keeping a deal together after inspection is often more important than adding another upgrade.

sections.h2: Spending to the comps, not to the house
sections.body:
Flint’s older homes often have enough charm to tempt a big renovation: oak trim, built-ins, leaded windows and fireplaces in Woodcroft, Mott Park and Carriage Town. Restoring those features is worthwhile when the comps support it. Refinishing floors, repairing plaster and keeping original woodwork can be cost-effective, and buyers in those neighborhoods notice.

The danger is overspending. Quartz counters, custom tile and high-end appliances may not add enough value in a market with modest comparable sales. We usually recommend a clean, functional kitchen with durable counters and standard appliances, an updated bathroom with simple tile and fixtures, new or refinished flooring, fresh paint and modern lighting. Spending on systems, roof and foundation first, then cosmetic items, protects you on the appraisal and the inspection. Our detailed scope lists each item and its cost so you can decide where to adjust. If the after-repair value cannot support the plan, we will tell you before you commit.

faqs.q: Which Flint neighborhoods are best for flips?
faqs.a: Owner-occupant demand is strongest in Woodcroft Estates, Mott Park, College Cultural, Glendale Hills and parts of Carriage Town, so those neighborhoods are where flips most often make sense. Even there, recent sales vary from street to street, and condition of surrounding properties affects appraisals. We look at the specific comps an appraiser would likely use before recommending a scope or finish level for your Flint property.

faqs.q: Do Flint buyers care about the plumbing?
faqs.a: Very much. Questions about pipes and water quality are among the first things buyers raise. A new service line, a complete interior repipe, new fixtures and a new water heater address those concerns and can help a sale go smoothly. We document the work with photos and permit records so the listing agent can share them with buyers and their inspectors.

faqs.q: Should I flip in Flint or in the suburbs?
faqs.a: It depends on your goals and the property. Suburbs like Grand Blanc, Fenton and Flushing often have stronger comps and more predictable buyer demand, but purchase prices are higher. Flint offers lower prices and less competition, but fewer neighborhoods support resale. We can scope properties in both and help you compare repair costs, after-repair values and likely buyer demand for each.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Flint, MI | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR contractor in Flint: complete, durable rehabs that hold rent and support the refinance on houses bought from the Land Bank, auctions and sellers.
brrrr.intro: Flint’s low purchase prices make the first step of BRRRR easy. The steps that come after are harder. Refinance appraisals are limited by thin comps, rehab costs stay stubbornly high compared with what houses sell for, and a stripped house can need every system replaced before it is rentable. A Flint BRRRR succeeds when the rehab is complete, durable and no bigger than it needs to be. Genstone Construction plans it that way. Before you commit, the free Pre-Offer Rehab Review totals the repairs and tests them against both the rent and the value a lender is likely to accept. During the rehab, a field manager runs licensed local trades from a line-item scope, permits run through the city, and draws release only when work is finished.

sections.h2: Being realistic about the Flint refinance
sections.body:
The weakest link in a Flint BRRRR is usually the appraisal. In much of the city, there are few recent sales of renovated homes, and many sales are cash transactions of distressed properties. An appraiser may struggle to support a high value even for excellent work. That means your plan should be built around a conservative after-repair value, with a refinance that still works if the number comes in lower than you hope.

Some investors in Flint lean on rental-income lending for the refinance. DSCR loans, such as those offered by Genstone Financial, focus on the property’s rent relative to its debt, though they still require an appraisal. Strong rents help, but the value still matters. We help by keeping the rehab focused: repairing everything a tenant and an appraiser would flag and avoiding finishes that add cost without changing the appraisal. Our itemized scope makes it easy to see what each dollar buys and adjust before work begins.

sections.h2: The Flint rehab package that holds up
sections.body:
A Flint rental that will be refinanced needs to be fully functional and easy to maintain. In practice, that usually means a complete interior repipe in PEX with new fixtures and a new water heater, a high-efficiency furnace with new ductwork where the old system was removed or damaged, and an updated electrical panel with grounded circuits. Roofs and gutters need to be sound, and the basement needs to be dry.

For finishes, we lean toward waterproof plank flooring through most of the house, washable semi-gloss paint, plywood-box cabinets that survive a leak, and faucets and lights a handyman can change in minutes. Windows that are rotted, broken or painted shut should be replaced, both for energy efficiency and to address lead hazards. Exterior doors should be steel, with good locks. This package does not try to impress, but it rents well, appraises in line with comparable rentals and keeps maintenance calls down.

sections.h2: Protecting the investment until it is leased
sections.body:
In Flint, the period between finishing the rehab and getting a tenant in place is risky. A newly renovated house with copper, a new furnace and new appliances is a target for theft if it sits empty. Some investors schedule appliance delivery and final fixture installation close to the lease start date, or keep the house monitored until it is occupied.

We help by planning the order of work so that high-value items are installed late in the project and the house is secured with solid doors, locks and window protection. Genstone Field Services can provide periodic property checks while the house is vacant. In winter, keeping the heat on is essential to protect new plumbing. Once a tenant moves in, the risk drops significantly. Coordinating with your property manager on marketing and showing schedules helps close the gap between final inspection and first rent payment, which also supports your refinance timeline.

faqs.q: Can I refinance a Flint rental with a DSCR loan?
faqs.a: Many investors do. A DSCR loan looks primarily at the property’s rent compared with its debt payments, which can be helpful in markets with limited comparable sales. An appraisal is still required, and loan terms vary by lender. Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans, but you can use any lender. Our detailed scope and photos help show the lender what was done to the property.

faqs.q: What rehab items matter most for a Flint rental?
faqs.a: Systems come first: plumbing, heating, electrical, roof and basement water. Tenants and appraisers both pay attention to those items. After that, durable flooring, sturdy cabinets, simple fixtures and solid exterior doors keep maintenance costs down. We focus the budget on items that keep the house rentable and appraisable rather than on high-end finishes that may not add value in Flint.

faqs.q: Do you work on houses bought at the Genesee County tax auction?
faqs.a: Yes, and they are some of the riskiest purchases to price. Tax-foreclosed homes have often sat empty for a long stretch, and bidders usually cannot get inside before the sale. In that situation we work from exterior photos, any listing images and what the neighborhood typically reveals, and give you a cost range rather than a single figure. Once you own the house, we walk every room and the basement and turn that range into a firm, itemized scope.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Flint, MI | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Flint rental renovation for single-family portfolios: repipes, secure doors, durable finishes and turns coordinated by one team across city and suburbs.
rental-renovation.intro: Single-family rentals make up a large share of occupied housing in many Flint neighborhoods, and the investors who own them face a specific set of problems: century-old systems, high theft risk when a house is empty, tenant concerns about water and a short list of contractors who show up reliably. Genstone Construction renovates and turns rental houses in Flint and the surrounding suburbs using a written standard that suits the city. Every address is priced on its own and supervised by a single field manager, with the labor done by licensed Genesee County trades. Between leases, our Field Services crews can inspect, maintain, ready the house and fix code items. Photos and updates go to you or your property manager, so you can manage the portfolio without driving every street yourself.

sections.h2: A Flint rental standard built around durability
sections.body:
A Flint rental standard should assume hard use and occasional vacancy. Flooring should be waterproof and easy to repair, which usually means plank flooring in most rooms. Walls should be painted in one neutral color with semi-gloss trim, so touch-ups are quick. Cabinets should be sturdy, with counters that shrug off a hot pan and a dropped can. Faucets and toilets should be common models whose cartridges and flappers your maintenance tech carries in the van.

On the mechanical side, the standard should specify a new or newer furnace, a new water heater, PEX supply lines with shutoff valves at each fixture and an electrical panel with enough capacity for modern appliances. Exterior doors should be steel with deadbolts, and basement windows should be secured. In many Flint houses, this standard replaces nearly every system, which is why the initial rehab is the expensive part. Once it is done, turns become simpler and maintenance calls fall, because the house is no longer relying on century-old components.

Tenants in Flint often ask about water before anything else. A rental with a documented service line replacement, a full interior repipe and new fixtures gives your property manager a clear answer. Some owners also provide a faucet-mounted or under-sink filter, which can reassure tenants. We keep photos and permit records of the plumbing work in your project file.

Lead paint is the other concern. Nearly all Flint rental houses were built before 1978, and federal disclosure rules apply. Peeling paint on windows, porches and trim is common in older homes. We address it during renovation with lead-safe work practices, window replacement where appropriate and stabilization of painted surfaces. Doing this work properly protects tenants, especially young children, and reduces liability for owners. It also prepares the house for any inspection the city or a housing program may require. Clear documentation makes it easier to answer tenant questions and respond to inspections.

Every turn in Flint is a window of risk. An empty house can be broken into, stripped or damaged by freezing in just a few days. Shortening that window is the best protection. Since the materials list is settled ahead of time, a turn can be priced from one walk-through, order materials and get crews in soon after the tenant moves out.

During cold months, keep the heat on in vacant rentals or winterize the plumbing immediately. A burst pipe in a vacant Flint house can cause damage that dwarfs the cost of a turn. Before winter, service furnaces, clean gutters, extend downspouts and check sump pumps. Genstone Field Services can schedule these checks across your portfolio. Securing doors and windows during vacancy also matters, along with avoiding leaving new appliances or materials exposed. Once a tenant is in place, the risk drops. Coordinating closely with your property manager on showings helps keep vacancy short and protects the investment.

faqs.q: Will you take on rentals in Burton, Flint Township and Grand Blanc too?
faqs.a: Yes. Our contractor network covers the city and the ring of communities around it, and many Flint-area portfolios mix the two. The difference is mostly paperwork: each suburb has its own building office and its own approach to rental property, so the permit plan follows the address. The work itself is often lighter in the suburbs, where a 1950s or 1960s ranch on a poured basement usually needs updating rather than the full system replacement common inside the city.

faqs.q: How do you handle repairs in a Flint rental that is occupied?
faqs.a: Through Genstone Field Services, which does maintenance and inspections in lived-in homes. Your property manager sets the visit, the tenant is told ahead of time when water or heat will be interrupted, and the interruption is kept as short as the repair allows, which matters in January. When the repair cuts into old painted trim or plaster, the crew sets up containment and cleans before leaving, since nearly every Flint rental has lead paint somewhere.

faqs.q: Are repairs from tenant damage covered by the warranty?
faqs.a: No. The one-year workmanship warranty is there for faults in how our contractors built or installed something, such as a supply line fitting that weeps or a door that was hung badly. Damage tenants cause and the ordinary wear of years of use are separate. For a Flint landlord, that is another reason to choose tough materials at the start, and when damage does happen we will photograph it and price the fix so your manager can deal with the deposit.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex and Small Multifamily Renovation in Flint, MI
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Flint duplex and 2–4 unit renovation: Carriage Town and Grand Traverse conversions, split meters, water costs, fire separation and phased work.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Duplex and Small Multifamily Renovation in Flint
multifamily-renovation.intro: Flint never built two-family flats on the scale Detroit did, so its small multifamily inventory is a patchwork: big Victorians in Carriage Town, the Grand Traverse District and Central Park that were cut into apartments, side-by-side duplexes on older east side streets, a few small brick walk-ups near downtown and the colleges. That variety means no two buildings share a standard scope. Genstone Construction evaluates each one starting with what the units depend on together, from the roof and foundation to the meters, stairs and fire separation, before pricing the interiors. Each building gets a field manager, licensed local contractors who pull city permits and a sequence that lets finished units start earning while others are still in progress.

sections.body:
The large houses closest to downtown were built for merchants, carriage makers and early auto executives, then divided into apartments as the city spread outward and those families moved to Woodcroft and the suburbs. In Carriage Town, the Grand Traverse District and around Central Park, it is common to find a Victorian with a unit on each floor and a third in the attic, reached by a narrow back stair or an exterior wooden staircase.

Those conversions were rarely done with modern codes in mind. Kitchens were added in bedrooms with no venting, electrical circuits were extended from a single service, and fire separation between units is often minimal. Some buildings have been vacant and damaged, which adds roof leaks, scrapping and fire risk to the list. Carriage Town is a historic neighborhood, and buyers and neighbors there value exterior restoration. We examine the structure, roof, stairs and electrical service before anything else, because those items affect every unit and often determine whether a building can be saved economically.

sections.h2: Meters, water bills and shared systems
sections.body:
Utility arrangements shape the economics of a Flint multi-unit more than the finishes do. Water bills in Flint have been high, and in buildings with one water meter, the owner typically pays them. Separate gas and electric meters let tenants pay their own heating and power costs, but older conversions often have a single meter or a mix of shared and separate services.

Splitting utilities usually means installing separate furnaces and water heaters, routing ductwork to each unit, upgrading and dividing the electrical service and coordinating with Consumers Energy for new gas and electric meters. Water separation is more complex and may not be practical in every building, so some owners include water in the rent and set rents accordingly. We price the options so you can compare them. At the same time, safety work usually needs to be done: fire-rated separation, self-closing doors, interconnected alarms and safe egress from upper units. All of this requires permits and inspections, which we coordinate through the city.

Many Flint multi-units are bought partially occupied or entirely vacant. In either case, the best approach is to bring units online one at a time. We begin with whatever the whole building needs to be safe and weather-tight: roof, gutters, foundation repairs, main electrical service, sewer lateral and the stairs and fire separation that serve every unit. With those items complete, the first unit can be finished, inspected and leased.

If a tenant is already living in the building, we schedule shared work in short, announced windows and keep their access, heat and water as uninterrupted as possible. Lead-safe practices are important because dust can travel through shared hallways and stairs. Once the first renovated unit is producing rent, the next can follow. This sequence reduces the time the building sits empty, which matters in Flint because vacant units invite theft and damage. It also spreads your capital out over time and lets early rents support later work.

faqs.q: Are Flint multi-unit buildings worth renovating?
faqs.a: Some are, especially near the colleges, downtown and in neighborhoods with stable rental demand. The economics depend on the condition of shared systems, utility arrangements and the rents each unit can command. Many converted Victorians need major work on roofs, stairs and electrical services. We price the building as a whole, so you can see whether the rents support the renovation before you buy.

faqs.q: Can I separate water meters in a Flint duplex?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but it depends on the building’s plumbing layout and the city’s requirements. In many older conversions, water lines are shared and separating them would require significant replumbing. Some owners choose to include water in the rent instead. We look at the plumbing and the cost of separation and help you compare it to including water as part of the lease.

faqs.q: Do historic rules affect multi-unit buildings in Carriage Town?
faqs.a: Carriage Town is one of Flint’s recognized historic neighborhoods, and depending on the building’s designation, exterior work such as windows, porches and siding may need review. Even where formal approval is not required, buyers and neighbors there tend to reward a faithful exterior. Before we price exterior work, we confirm with the city what applies to the specific address, then specify materials and details that fit the house so the review, if there is one, is not a surprise.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Flint, MI | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor in Flint: realistic bids for Mott Park, Woodcroft and Civic Park homes, consultant coordination and draw records.
fha-203k.intro: The FHA 203(k) loan can help a Flint buyer purchase a house that needs work and finance the renovation in the same mortgage. That matters in a city where many affordable homes need new plumbing, heating or roofs before they are comfortable to live in. The program has a hard limit, though: the finished value has to support the loan. Genstone carries FHA 203(k) contractor certification, and our job on a Flint file is to make the bid realistic and the documentation clean. We prepare itemized bids, coordinate with HUD consultants on Standard loans, schedule draw inspections and keep permit records from the city. A single field manager follows the house from bid to final draw while licensed Flint-area trades do the building.

sections.body:
The best Flint candidates are structurally sound homes in neighborhoods where buyers want to live and where appraisers can find comparable sales. Mott Park, College Cultural, Woodcroft Estates and Glendale Hills fit that description. A 1930s brick house in Mott Park with an old furnace, galvanized pipes and a dated kitchen is a classic Limited 203(k). A Woodcroft Tudor may need roofing, masonry and window work that pushes the scope higher.

Civic Park houses are another option. Their compact colonials and bungalows can make good starter homes, but many need foundation, porch and roof work along with updated systems. Homes on streets with many vacant properties are harder, because appraisals there may not support the full cost of renovation. Houses that have been stripped or burned typically need more work than the loan can finance relative to their value. Our review answers one blunt question before the buyer spends money on an appraisal: will the finished house be worth what it costs to buy and fix?

For non-structural work, the Limited 203(k) applies, capped at $75,000. It suits Flint houses that need new plumbing, a furnace and water heater, electrical updates, a roof without structural repair, windows, kitchen and bath remodels, flooring and paint. Because Flint homes are often moderately priced, many renovation budgets fall well within that limit.

The Standard 203(k) applies when structural work is involved or when the project is more complex. That version starts at a $5,000 minimum, and a HUD-approved consultant writes the work up and checks each draw. Projects that involve repairing bowed basement walls, rebuilding porches on new footings, reframing fire-damaged areas or reconfiguring a converted house typically fall here. Additional inspection requirements apply once repairs exceed the $15,000 threshold. In Flint, the decision often turns on the basement and on whether there is any fire or structural damage. Our scope identifies structural items clearly so the lender can choose the right program early.

Flint 203(k) files benefit from extra documentation, because appraisers and lenders want to see clear evidence of improvements in a market with modest values. Our bids list each repair with its labor, materials and permit costs, and we provide photos of the existing conditions that justify each item.

After closing, renovation funds are held in escrow and released in draws. A Flint draw is released only after the consultant or the lender’s inspector has seen the finished stage in person. Our field manager provides photos, confirms that the related city inspection has passed and collects lien waivers from the contractors who were paid. Because water is a sensitive topic in Flint, we document the interior repipe and any service line information carefully, which helps both the buyer and future buyers. If hidden problems appear, such as a cracked drain under the basement floor or charred framing behind paneling, we submit a change order with photos for approval before proceeding. Buyers receive regular updates throughout the project.

faqs.q: Can a 203(k) loan be used in Civic Park?
faqs.a: Yes, if the property qualifies and the finished value supports the loan. Those compact 1919-era houses can make good first homes, though many carry porch, roof and basement repairs in addition to dated systems. We look at the condition and recent sales in the area and tell you whether the renovation makes sense for the expected value before you commit to appraisals and consultant fees.

faqs.q: Can a full repipe be financed in a Flint 203(k)?
faqs.a: Yes. Replacing interior supply piping is an eligible repair, and in older Flint homes it is often near the top of the list. We bid the repipe as its own line, including new shutoff valves, fixtures and the water heater, and photograph the old galvanized lines before they come out. That record helps the consultant approve the draw, shows the appraiser the improvement and gives the buyer something to hand the next owner years from now.

faqs.q: When should a Flint buyer bring a 203(k) contractor in?
faqs.a: Before the offer, if possible. A short visit lets us spot the things that change the loan, like a bowed basement wall, a porch on failing piers or signs of an old fire, and give the agent a working figure. Once the purchase agreement is signed, we turn that into the formal bid the lender needs and, on Standard files, reconcile it with the consultant’s write-up so the closing is not held up waiting on paperwork.

reo-renovation.title: REO Property Renovation in Flint, MI | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: Flint REO and bank-owned renovation for servicers, banks and GSEs: stripped systems, fire risk, freeze damage and utility restoration, fully documented.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovation in Flint
reo-renovation.intro: A foreclosed house in Flint can lose value faster than almost anywhere else in Michigan. Left empty, it may be stripped, burned or frozen before the asset manager has finished reviewing the file. Genstone Construction stabilizes and renovates REO homes in Flint and across Genesee County for servicers, banks, REITs, funds and the GSEs, which count Genstone among their preferred contractors. Our bids follow the formats and approval steps those asset managers already use. Our team documents conditions with photos, prepares line-item bids, assigns a field manager and coordinates licensed local contractors under city permits. Genstone Field Services can secure, winterize and inspect properties from takeover through sale, keeping the condition from sliding further.

sections.body:
In Flint, securing an REO property is the first and most urgent task. Vacant houses are routinely entered and stripped of copper, furnaces, water heaters and wiring. Unsecured houses can also become sites for dumping, squatting and fire, which can spread to neighboring properties. The faster the property is secured, the more of its value is preserved.

Genstone Field Services can change locks, replace damaged doors, secure basement windows, board openings where necessary and post the property according to the client’s requirements. In winter, the plumbing should be drained and winterized immediately if the heat is off. We document the condition at takeover with photos, including any existing damage from scrapping, fire or freezing, so the asset manager has a baseline for later decisions. Periodic inspections can be scheduled to check for new break-ins or damage while the bid is reviewed. These steps cost far less than repairing a house that was stripped after takeover.

sections.h2: Scoping repairs in a thin market
sections.body:
Many Flint REO properties will sell to investors rather than owner-occupants, and the repair strategy should reflect that. In neighborhoods with strong owner-occupant demand, such as Mott Park, College Cultural and Woodcroft Estates, it may make sense to repair the property to a financeable condition so it can be sold to a buyer using FHA or conventional financing. That typically includes restoring heat, plumbing and electrical service, repairing roof leaks, addressing deteriorated paint and correcting safety hazards.

In areas where most buyers pay cash, a lighter scope focused on stabilization, cleanup and safety may produce a better net result. We can price both approaches so the asset manager can compare them with the broker’s pricing. Restoring utilities in a stripped house requires coordination with Consumers Energy for gas and electric service and with the city for water, along with permits and inspections. We build those steps into the schedule because they often control the timeline.

sections.h2: Paperwork that holds up on a Flint REO file
sections.body:
With modest values and fast-changing conditions, a Flint REO file has to explain itself to anyone who opens it later. Each of our bids breaks the work into individual lines, keeps labor and materials apart, includes disposal and dumpster costs from the outset and pins a photo to every line. Long-vacant Flint houses often come with a basement and garage full of debris, so leaving the trash-out off the bid would understate the real cost.

Once work starts, the field manager reports against those same lines, so the asset manager can see what is done and what is not without reading through narrative notes. Surprises are handled in writing: if drywall removal exposes charred studs or a camera shows a collapsed lateral, the change order arrives with pictures before the extra work begins. Contractors sign lien waivers when paid. Field Services keeps lawn care, re-securing, winterization and inspections on the same calendar as the renovation, which closes the gaps between vendors that vacant Flint houses tend to exploit.

faqs.q: How soon can a Flint REO be secured after takeover?
faqs.a: As soon as the asset manager authorizes access, Genstone Field Services can be on site to re-key, repair or replace damaged doors, close up basement windows and board openings to the client’s specification. The same visit produces a dated photo record of the condition at takeover. In the cold months, the plumbing is drained and winterized right away. Speed matters more in Flint than in most markets, because an open house can lose its copper and furnace within days.

faqs.q: Should a Flint REO be fully renovated before it is listed?
faqs.a: That depends on who is likely to buy it. On streets in Mott Park, College Cultural or Woodcroft Estates, repairing to the point where an FHA or conventional buyer can finance the house usually widens the pool and lifts the price. In parts of the city where nearly every sale is cash, stabilization, cleanup and safety repairs often net more. We price both versions side by side so the asset manager can weigh them against the broker’s opinion of value.

faqs.q: Can utilities be restored on a stripped Flint REO?
faqs.a: Yes, though it takes more steps than a simple reconnection. Missing supply piping, gas lines, wiring and sometimes the meter base have to be replaced and inspected under city permits before Consumers Energy will restore gas and electric service and the city will turn the water back on. We include each step in the bid and schedule, because utility restoration usually controls when the rest of the renovation can move forward.
